toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Turnaround doubled mainly because of a control change on 1 April. After an audit found overpayments, adjusters' sign-off limit dropped from $10,000 to $2,500. Claims of $2,500–$10,000 (about 53% of closures) now wait for one of three team leads. Time pending approval went from 0.7 to 16 days in that band. Every other stage is flat, including indexing and investigation. Claims under $2,500 and over $10,000 barely changed. The team-lead tray grew from 11 to 455 items. The leads approve about 199 a week against about 212 arriving. Nobody assessed the workload impact before the change.

The hail event, the lost senior adjusters and Quillfast don't explain the rise in the data. The complaint increase is partly a logging change, so don't treat it as proof of delay. I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%). Whether the lower limit actually cuts overpayments is unmeasured.

Don't approve the four contractors or the imaging switch back. Don't discipline the team leads. Don't drop the control unilaterally. Instead, agree with Internal Audit on added approval capacity, such as certifying senior adjusters as second approvers. Keep a second review on every claim in the band and track pending-approval time weekly. Hold permanent limits until the December re-test.
